, for the first time, we propose a deep learning architecture for the cross-domain matching problem and we collect a large real dataset with more than 27,000 facial images of selfies, ID documents and passports from the database of a major Brazilian bank, with 13,501 subjects.
, in this paper, we present an innovative approach for the problem of cross-domain face matching, with a large real dataset and an extensive evaluation of the proposed solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the usage of deep features extracted by CNNs is a very promising approach to deal with the cross-domain face verification problem.

the proposed approach is able to achieve state-of-the-art results for cross-domain face matching, with accuracy rates of 94.5% on the proposed dataset, 94.1% on the LFW dataset, 95.7% on the PubFig dataset and 95.3% on the YouTube Face dataset.
, even with the differences between the two domains (ID and selfies), the use of deep features extracted by CNNs is a feasible approach to solve the cross-domain face verification problem.
